items.title: Man City's Maresca 'very happy' after Ipswich win
items.summary: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats” but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first manager in history to win his first seven games in charge of a team. Ipswich were the latest victims but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules .

items.title: European football: Baena late strike for Atlético puts pressure on Barcelona
items.summary: Simeone’s side move two points behind La Liga champions I’d have left Real Madrid if I were Vinícius, says Mourinho Álex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atlético Madrid a 1-0 win at Espanyol and put pressure on the La Liga leaders, Barcelona. Diego Simeone’s side are second, two points behind Hansi Flick’s champions, who visit third-placed Real Betis later on. Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella.

items.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
items.summary: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of.

items.title: Scottish Premiership: Kiltie double sinks Motherwell to lift Kilmarnock
items.summary: Kilmarnock move off bottom with 3-2 win Hibs 1-2 Falkirk; Aberdeen 3-1 St Mirren Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell . Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian. Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head.

items.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again
items.summary: Mukasa’s first-half goal enough to beat leaders Swansea Canaries suffer sixth straight loss; Watford beat Charlton West Ham ended Swansea’s four-match winning streak with a 1-0 away victory that reduced the gap at the top of the Championship to a single point. Divine Mukasa’s calm first-half finish proved the difference, with the result putting the Hammers second, within a point of Swansea, who lost at home for the first time since April. Swansea had made their best start since 1923 by winning seven and drawing two of their opening 10 games.
